data.title: DTC E-commerce
data.tagline: Let product, brand feeling, and buying information work together toward a decision
data.description: DTC, or direct-to-consumer, describes a business model rather than a visual style. This example shows a common branded e-commerce pattern: the product leads visually while price, options, reviews, delivery, and the purchase action remain easy to understand. Lifestyle imagery and editorial typography can create desire, but the page cannot behave like a lookbook alone.

use: Beauty, fashion, food, and lifestyle brands with visually distinctive products and stories
Brands selling directly to customers , where the website must express identity and convert
Products that benefit from material, process, or usage guidance to reduce uncertainty
Businesses driven by repeat and bundle purchases , where recommendations and sets belong naturally in the journey
avoid: Interrupt with offers before showing the product ; repeated popups damage judgment and brand confidence
Use beautiful images without buying facts , leaving price, options, and delivery hard to find
Label every item a must-have bestseller ; without difference, the language cannot help anyone choose
Place the mobile purchase action far away ; it should remain easy to reach through longer content

data.agentPrompt: DTC e-commerce product page, high-quality product and lifestyle photography, editorial typography, warm off-white canvas with a restrained brand color, price, options, reviews, delivery and add-to-bag action placed together, balancing brand expression with shopping efficiency
